name: hcapp_selectSong
description: Records a song selection for an event in the interactive songbook. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 76, @param NULL — device-secret token). Gate: the caller must hold a HasherEventMap row for the event with RsvpState >= 2 (Maybe/Yes) and Removed = 0 — errorCode 1283, errorType 3 otherwise; no kennel role is needed. All selections are retained in HC.SongSession for history — this does not replace a previous selection. Returns three rowsets on success: a compact envelope, adHocData with song details for the Flutter caller plus metadata for the Azure Function fan-out, and a third rowset of FCM recipients (RSVP'd Maybe/Yes or checked in, not marked absent, mobile devices only, honouring the event/kennel notification preference) for the Azure Function to push a visible notification to. New feature — no HC5 equivalent.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth for auth resolution. No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived auth token validated against DeviceSecret. No SQL default.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Event the song is being selected for. Required — null or zero-UUID triggers validation error (errorCode 1281, errorType 2). No SQL default.

parameters.name: songId
parameters.description: Song being selected. Must exist in HC.Song with Removed = 0. Required — null or zero-UUID triggers validation error (errorCode 1282, errorType 2). Song-not-found returns errorCode 1284, errorType 2. No SQL default.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Compact error envelope on auth, validation, RSVP check, song-not-found, or insert failure: { success=0, errorCode, errorType }. Followed by StandardErrorResult at index 1. Mutually exclusive with SuccessEnvelope.

rowsets.name: SuccessEnvelope
rowsets.description: Compact success envelope: { success=1, errorCode=NULL, errorType=NULL }. Mutually exclusive with ErrorEnvelope. Followed by AdHocData at index 1 and FcmRecipients at index 2.
Returned at index 1 alongside the ErrorEnvelope (index 0) on any error. Mutually exclusive with AdHocData rowset.

rowsets.name: AdHocData
rowsets.description: Single row of non-sync data for the Flutter caller and the Azure Function. adHocDataId = 1 (constant sentinel per the adHocDataId pattern). Contains the song title, selector name, event/song IDs (lowercase), and the count of push recipients pre-computed at insert time. Mutually exclusive with StandardErrorResult rowset.

columns.name: adHocDataId
columns.description: Always 1. Sentinel value per the HC6 adHocDataId pattern — signals this is a non-sync data rowset.

columns.name: songTitle
columns.description: HC.Song.SongName for the selected song — used in the Flutter snackbar and push notification body.

columns.name: selectedByName
columns.description: Display name of the caller resolved via COALESCE(NULLIF(HashName,''), NULLIF(DisplayName,''), NULLIF(FirstName,''), 'Someone').

columns.name: eventId
columns.description: The event UUID as lowercase NVARCHAR(40). Used by the Azure Function to scope the push.

columns.name: songId
columns.description: The selected song UUID as lowercase NVARCHAR(40). Used by the Azure Function to include in the push payload.

columns.name: recipientCount
columns.description: Pre-computed count of distinct mobile FCM recipients who will receive the push notification. Matches the rowset 2 WHERE clause exactly.

rowsets.name: FcmRecipients
rowsets.description: One row per distinct FCM token for mobile devices eligible to receive the song-selected push notification. Consumed by the Azure Function for fan-out — not parsed by the Flutter client. Excludes users who have set notification preference to 'ignore' (2) entirely; excludes 'mute' (3) unless the user is physically at the run (AttendenceState 20-39). Effective preference cascades: event-level if non-zero, otherwise kennel-level.

columns.name: FcmToken
columns.description: HC.Device.FcmToken — Firebase Cloud Messaging token for the recipient device.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: HC.Device.UserId cast to lowercase NVARCHAR(40) — the recipient user ID.

columns.name: showNotification
columns.description: Always 1. Signals the Azure Function to send a visible (alert) notification, not a silent data-only push (iOS throttles silent pushes to ~3/hour).

sideEffects: INSERT HC.SongSession (EventId, SongId, SelectedByUserId, SelectedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME()) — one row per call, inside the SP's only transaction (lines 170-175).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on validation (1281 eventId, 1282 songId, 1284 song not found; type 2), RSVP gate (1283; type 3) and insert failure (1285; type 5). ValidateAppAuth logs its own auth failures.
No push is sent by the SP: rowset 2 is the recipient list the Azure Function fans out to.

codeSmells.detail: Lines 3-6: @deviceId, @accessToken, @eventId and @songId have no SQL default. A client that omits one gets 'expects parameter ... which was not supplied' before the body runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row — and the SP's own 1281/1282 'Missing event/song' paths are unreachable. Give every parameter a default (= NULL) and keep the NULL checks.

codeSmells.issue: Most of the body runs outside TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Only the INSERT (lines 169-186) is wrapped. The kennel lookup (123-124), the recipient COUNT (127-156), the display-name resolution (159-166) and, after the CATCH, the adHocData and recipient SELECTs (189-238) all run bare. A runtime error in any of them (timeout, deadlock on HasherEventMap) is a raw HTTP 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'TRY/CATCH is mandatory'). The recipient query at 206-238 is the heaviest statement in the SP and the one most likely to time out.

HC.SongSession.Removed is declared BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (db/hc6/app/archive/HC6.SongSession.migration.sql). The project standard is SMALLINT; the companion hcapp_getCurrentSong filters WHERE ss.Removed = 0, which works by implicit conversion, and any Dart fromJson of this column must use the BIT idiom (== true || == 1).

codeSmells.issue: Gate and audience disagree about checked-in hashers
codeSmells.detail: The caller gate (line 93-96) requires RsvpState >= 2, so a hasher who was checked in at the circle (AttendenceState >= 20) without ever RSVPing is refused with 1283, yet the recipient list (line 222) includes exactly those hashers. The audience test '(RsvpState >= 2 OR AttendenceState >= 20) AND AttendenceState <> 10' is the one the gate should use too.

codeSmells.issue: recipientCount pre-computed with a separate COUNT query that duplicates rowset 2 logic
codeSmells.detail: Lines 128-156 and 206-238 are two hand-copied WHERE clauses. If one is edited without the other, adHocData.recipientCount diverges from the rows the Azure Function actually receives. A single inline table-valued function or a #temp populated once would remove the copy.
Line 35: cosmetic inconsistency with the other app SPs; the CATCH logs the right name.

breakingChanges: 1.1.0 (2026-09-25): no rowset change. Recipients and recipientCount skip deleted hashers (Hasher.Removed = 1) and retired device rows (Device.removed = 1).
1.2.0 (2026-10-13): contract corrections only — envelope success typed INT, parameters marked as having no SQL default, auth/gate documented, smells re-pointed at current line numbers.
